mechanism_narrative: The sharp rebound in WORKPLACES from -25.3 to -8.6 within two weeks signals a resumption of commuting and lunch-trip routines, which should raise RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as office-linked discretionary visits recover.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not average above its prior 28-day mean over the next 28 days while WORKPLACES remains above the t-2w level for at least two of the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL stays above 10 points while TRANSIT remains below -15 points, households substitute toward local, nearby shopping trips and reduce long-distance travel, pushing RETAIL_REC lower over the next two to four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL above 10 and TRANSIT below -15 for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises relative to the last 28 days even though RESIDENTIAL stays above 10 and TRANSIT stays below -15 for two straight weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained recovery in PARKS after a negative weekly shock indicates renewed leisure mobility that competes with indoor retail visits, so RETAIL_REC should remain lower over the next week if PARKS stays near or above baseline.
candidate_trigger: PARKS crosses from below 0 to above 0 on a weekly mean
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 7 days after PARKS crosses above zero and remains positive for the week.

mechanism_narrative: During holiday shopping periods, concurrent strength in GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC indicates broader trip-making intensity; if grocery demand stays elevated and retail is not yet saturated, RETAIL_REC should increase over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below its prior 28-day mean even though GROCERY_PHARM stays at or above 9 points for at least three of the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A further drop in TRANSIT from its current depressed level indicates stronger movement suppression or travel caution, which reduces incidental retail visits and should push RETAIL_REC down within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls by at least 3 points week-on-week from a level below -15
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last 28-day mean after TRANSIT drops at least 3 points week-on-week from below -15.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both recover together, the same people generate more chained errands and after-work shopping, so RETAIL_REC should turn upward over the next four weeks; the signal fails if only one of the two improves.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve over the next 28 days when WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rise by at least 5 points from their t-0w levels.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS continues to fall while RESIDENTIAL remains elevated, leisure time is shifting indoors and neighborhood substitution is weak, which should keep RETAIL_REC below its recent average over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS below -5 while RESIDENTIAL stays above 10
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days despite PARKS staying below -5 and RESIDENTIAL staying above 10.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in GROCERY_PHARM above its current plateau, while TRANSIT remains suppressed, implies demand is being redirected to essential trips rather than discretionary shopping, so RETAIL_REC should stay flat or weaken over the next month.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises above 12 while TRANSIT remains below -15
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC exceeds its prior 28-day mean over the next 28 days even though GROCERY_PHARM rises above 12 and TRANSIT stays below -15.
